outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Case Background and Procedural Posture
outline.description: This chapter establishes the factual context of the employment relationship and details the evolution of the litigation from the initial allegation to the summary judgment appeal. It highlights the critical stipulations entered by the parties regarding monetary compensation, which created unique jurisdictional challenges.
subtopics: Facts of Employment: Cohen's role as an hourly licensed attorney document reviewer starting in 2018
The Trigger Event: Consilio's August 2019 elimination of premium overtime pay via email notification
Litigation Initiation: Cohen filing suit on behalf of himself and a putative class under state wage laws
Statutory Basis for Claims: Overview of allegations under MPWA, MFLSA, and MWTA
Critical Stipulations: Agreement that overtime wages and liquidated damages were paid in full ($256,010.01 total)
Procedural Status Disagreement: Parties' inability to agree on entitlement to civil penalties versus wages

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Standard of Review and Legal Framework for Summary Judgment
outline.description: Before addressing specific merits, this chapter defines the appellate standard applied by the Eighth Circuit. It clarifies how 'de novo' review functions in the context of summary judgment motions and sets the evidentiary burden placed on non-moving parties during judicial interpretation.
subtopics: 'De Novo' Review Defined: Examining evidence without deference to lower court findings
'Light Most Favorable': How inferences are drawn strictly toward Cohen as the non-movant
Elements Required for Summary Judgment Success by Defendant: Absence of genuine disputes of material fact + entitlement to judgment as a matter of law
Role of Judicial Interpretation vs. Fact-Finding in Wage Law Cases

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Analysis Under the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act (MPWA)
outline.description: This chapter analyzes why individual employees cannot sue directly for 'average daily wage penalties.' It explores statutory construction principles used by the court to distinguish between private rights to prosecute wage claims versus administrative powers reserved exclusively for the State Commissioner.
subtopics: Purposeful Distinction Between Private Actions and Administrative Enforcement:
- Textual analysis distinguishing § 181.101 from other MPWA sections granting private penalty rights
"Legislative Intent" Doctrine: Inferring intent based on contrast with neighboring statutes (§§ 181.13/14)
- Requirement for Commissioner involvement prior to penalty assessment
- Distribution mechanism ensuring penalties flow through official channels
-- Precedent Application: Citing *Allan* and *Milner* to confirm exclusivity
